title: Nepal Maintains 'BB-minus' Country Rating by Fitch - Ratopati
description: Nepal Maintains 'BB-minus' Country Rating by Fitch  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal's 'BB-minus' country rating has continued. In the report published by international rating agency 'Fitch' on November 12, 2026 (Thursday), Nepal received the same rating as the last 2 times.

The latest review report prepared by the team of analysts George-Su and Benedict Craven from Fitch's Hong Kong office has kept Nepal's long-term rating regarding foreign and local currency issuers stable at 'BB-minus'. Similarly, the short-term rating has been maintained at 'B' and the country ceiling also at 'BB-minus'.

Receiving a 'BB-minus' rating is considered respectable for a developing and least developed country like Nepal.

This rating shows that the country's economy and debt repayment capacity are secure and balanced for the immediate future, but it also indicates the risk of financial imbalance if there is major political instability, natural disaster, or economic recession in the country.

Nepal has faced two major disasters in the recent past. Due to the Jenji movement on September 9 and 10 last year, the country's business environment was devastated.

On the other hand, the flood that occurred on September 10 this year not only increased Nepal's environmental risk but also increased the reconstruction liability by more than 700 billion.

Chartered Accountant Anallraj Bhattarai says that succeeding in maintaining the old rating again by overcoming these disasters is a great achievement. He states that Fitch has provided the new rating based on Nepal's latest situation and economic data.

“The country had to face two globally discussed disasters in the last 12/13 months. Even amidst this grip, Nepal's rating not falling is a positive sign in itself,” Bhattarai said, “The rating remaining stable in such adverse conditions indicates that the situation has not worsened and there is a possibility of further improvement in the coming days.”

Nepal first received a 'BB-minus' rating on November 21, 2024. Subsequently, the same rating continued in the review held on November 18, 2025. Nepal has also managed to remain in the same category in the third review published in November 2026.

Strong Basis for Maintaining Rating: External Sector and Monetary Stability

The rating by international rating agencies mainly includes two indicators. First, factual indicators and second, quantitative indicators. Bhattarai says that factual indicators have helped maintain Nepal's rating this time.

Especially, the stability of the external sector has provided great stability to Nepal's economy. With the high and continuous inflow of remittances, Nepal has foreign exchange reserves to sustain 20 to 22 months of goods and services imports.

Nepal's current foreign debt structure is also not unfavorable. With debt being only around 43/44 percent of the gross domestic product, and only half of that debt being foreign, it is a comfortable situation.

Moreover, the debt taken by Nepal in foreign currency is low, and the existing debt is not expensive commercial loans but concessional loans obtained from bodies like the World Bank, Asian Development Bank, and friendly nations. Bhattarai says that since foreign direct investment (FDI) is low, the risk of capital outflow at high rates during a crisis is low, which has also helped stabilize the rating.

Monetary and financial sector policies have also helped maintain the rating. Although the impact of recession and protests in the economy was expected to cause a sharp increase in banks' non-performing loans, the average bad loan being around 5/6 percent even in the first quarter of the current fiscal year shows that the overall system is under control. Similarly, low interest rates and adequate liquidity are estimated to support business recovery, as stated in the report.

Furthermore, Bhattarai's analysis suggests that Nepal's success in pushing back the deadline for graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status by three years has ensured continuity in the concessions received in international markets and exports, maintaining trade continuity, balancing government revenue and GDP, and efforts towards policy reforms have also helped to withstand negative pressure.

Three Reasons Hindering Graduation

Although quantitative indicators have tried to pull up Nepal's rating, Bhattarai clarifies that Nepal has not been able to move from 'BB-minus' to 'BB' due to qualitative aspects and structural weaknesses.

According to him, Nepal is still weak in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues. The lack of perceived good governance at the general level and the weak implementation of legal reforms are the main obstacles to rating improvement.

Nepal's limitation to around 31 points in the World Bank's Governance Index has also negatively impacted the rating.

Failure to fully convince the international community about corruption control and policy stability has prevented the 'minus' sign in the rating from being removed.

Fitch's report also indicates that if good governance and ESG indicators could be improved, Nepal would have reached the 'BB' category this year.

In addition, Nepal is on the grey list of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), an international body for anti-money laundering. Nepal has a deadline until February 2027 to get out of this list. CA Bhattarai says that this has also created negative pressure on the rating, and being on the international watch list for human trafficking has also prevented the rating from upgrading.

The potential financial and reconstruction liability of approximately 700 billion rupees created by climate change and floods and landslides has also put pressure on the government treasury, and its impact is seen in the upgrade, he says.

How Does Fitch Rate Countries?

Fitch assesses a country's overall performance based on its Sovereign Rating Criteria updated on April 27, 2026, and Country Ceiling Criteria from July 2023.

Initially, a base score is calculated by analyzing 18 economic and financial indicators through the Sovereign Rating Model (SRM), and qualitative adjustments are made through Qualitative Overlay (QO).

Among the four main pillars of SRM, structural characteristics account for the largest weight of 53.7 percent. Among these, the World Bank's Governance Index alone carries a weight of 22.1 percent, followed by share in global GDP at 14.5 percent, GDP per capita at 11.7 percent, debt restructuring period at 4.3 percent, and broad money supply at 1.1 percent.

The remaining pillars include public finance at 19.1 percent, external finance at 17.3 percent, and macroeconomic performance and policy at 9.8 percent.

For the rating committee that convenes between July and December, average and projected data for three years, focusing on the current year 2026, are used. According to Fitch's criteria, if the long-term rating is BB-minus, the short-term rating is automatically B.

Fitch Uses 'Climate Vulnerability Signal' in Rating Process

Fitch also tests physical and transitional climate risks such as floods, droughts, and temperature increases through an indicator called Climate Vulnerability Signal (Climate.VS).

If the risk indicator for 2035 is 50 or above, there is a provision to make further detailed analysis and adjust the rating up or down through qualitative adjustments.

The stability maintained at the 'BB-minus' rating for the past three years is expected to send a positive message to foreign investors, says Bhattarai.

The economy appearing stable despite major political movements and natural disasters has strengthened Nepal's debt repayment capacity and confidence in its financial system, he says. This will help attract foreign investment and expand access to international capital markets in the future.

This situation has increased the possibility of Nepal's upgrade in the upcoming rating. The government is currently preparing to amend 59 laws and facilitate business operations. Analysts say that if these laws are reformed and Nepal can get out of the FATF grey list, it will provide a strong basis for Nepal's rating to rise in the next review.

title: Children born abroad to Nepali mothers with unidentified fathers can now obtain citizenship through self-declaration - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Children born abroad to Nepali mothers with unidentified fathers can now obtain citizenship through self-declaration  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Representational sketch

Kathmandu, November 15

Children born abroad to Nepali mothers whose fathers have not been identified can now obtain naturalised Nepali citizenship through a formal self-declaration process.

The provision has come into implementation following the fifth amendment to the Nepal Citizenship Regulations, 2026, which includes prescribed formats for self-declarations by both the applicants and their mothers.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has made the amended regulations public, outlining the declarations required from individuals seeking citizenship under this provision.

According to the prescribed format, applicants must declare that they were born abroad to a Nepali citizen mother, have permanently resided in Nepal, have not acquired foreign citizenship or a passport, and have no identified father.

Section 5(5b) of the Nepal Citizenship Act, 2006, provides for naturalised citizenship for individuals who meet these conditions and whose mothers also make the required self-declaration.

Although the provision was already included in the Act, the formal procedure and prescribed format for the declarations had not been clearly established. The fifth amendment to the Citizenship Regulations addresses this gap by incorporating the format in Schedule 7(c).

Under the amended regulations, applicants must provide their full name, date of birth, signature and the date of declaration. They are also required to provide their right and left thumbprints. The authorised official overseeing the declaration must likewise record their name, designation, signature and date.

The regulations also prescribe a separate declaration format for mothers. They must confirm that their child was born abroad to a Nepali citizen mother, has permanently resided in Nepal, has not obtained foreign citizenship or a passport, and that the child’s father remains unidentified.

Mothers are required to provide their citizenship certificate number, issuing district, date of issue and national identity number.

Both the applicant and the mother must affirm that the information provided is true and acknowledge that they will be liable under the law if their declarations are found to be false.

The prescribed format for the declarations is linked to Rule 7(1b)(e) of the amended regulations.

title: Film Promotion Stunts Backfire in Nepal - Ratopati
description: Film Promotion Stunts Backfire in Nepal  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. In the Nepali film industry, the trend of adopting 'promotion stunts' to attract audience attention has been on the rise lately. However, such stunts, carried out without understanding sensitivity and subject matter, often cause more harm than good to the film. A recent example is the film 'Kakakiki'.

Towards the end of the trailer launch event held on Saturday, four to five police personnel suddenly entered the hall and took director Bikky Agarwal, along with actors Gauri Malla, Manoj Gajurel, and Shishir Wandel, into a police van. As the video went viral, curiosity grew on social media about 'Why were the artists arrested?'. After the social media buzz, the unit stated that it was not real and was a 'promotion stunt'.

Following the production unit's response, the act is now facing widespread criticism. This stunt, done for promotion of the film set to be released on November 25, is now 'backfiring'.

Such promotion stunts in Nepal are proving to be counterproductive. The recently released film 'Panch Pandav' also failed due to a stunt. Although the first look showing actress Iva Giri as Draupadi received praise, the song 'Raja Chahia Chha' caused controversy. In the song, Iva, referred to as Draupadi, was shown performing an item dance in a casino, and Haribansha Acharya, playing Yudhishthira, was shown playing cards. The depiction of a proud character like Draupadi in a 'bar dancer' style was seen as an attack on religious sanctity, leading to calls for boycott. Some chief district officers even drew the attention of the Home Ministry and showed interest in the screening. Despite the director saying, 'This is not the end, but a strong beginning,' the controversy affected the film's business.

The films 'Masterni' and 'Mami' starring actress Priyanka Karki were also affected by incorrect promotion styles. For 'Masterni', a song made with Durgesh Thapa used ambiguous lyrics and gestures like 'If you want to learn math, come home in the evening,' which were criticized for attacking the professional sensitivity of teachers. Although Priyanka apologized, the business declined, and both continue to face criticism. Similarly, for the promotion of 'Mami', her act of roaming around New Road scaring people as a ghost also received negative reactions, impacting the business.

Films by singers Ramkrishna Dhakal and Prakash Saput were also harmed by controversial statements. Dhakal's claim in a television interview during the promotion of his production 'Malati Mangale' that he drove Ravi Lamichhane away in his own car after his release from jail led to a barrage of insults calling him a 'cooperative fraud,' and the film flopped. Similarly, Prakash Saput's praise for former Prime Minister and UML Chairman KP Oli, hoping it would benefit 'Basanta,' led to the film being tagged as 'UML.' Calls for boycott were made, and the audience did not support it.

However, not all promotion stunts are unsuccessful. In 'Gauthali,' actress Simran Khadka's promotion in a rural setting around Patan carrying a basket, and actor Arun Kshetri's television interview portraying an autistic character, earned praise and benefited the business. Similarly, Dipendra Lama's directorial 'Chha Maya Chhapakai' became commercially successful with a promotion stunt involving a parody of Durgesh Thapa's Teej song 'Bich Bich Ma' filmed in a tall building in Radhe Radhe, Bhaktapur.

Looking at the overall picture, 'promotion stunts' seem to have caused harm to many.

Senior journalist and director Vijayaratna Tuladhar believes that promotion styles that are appropriate to the subject matter and are dignified are more beneficial for films than cheap popularity. Tuladhar argues that the stunt of arresting actors like Gauri Malla and Manoj Gajurel misused the country's police administration. He says, 'In film promotions, there are examples in Hollywood and Bollywood where artists have presented themselves in getups suitable to the subject matter. For instance, in the promotion of the film 'Border,' which was based on an army background, all the actors came in army uniforms. But there is no need to stage a drama or a farce as if someone is genuinely arrested without reason.'

Tuladhar states that if stunts are necessary for promotion, they should be creative. He emphasizes that if the film itself is strong, other creative methods should be adopted instead of such negative promotions. 'Such stunts do not directly benefit the film, but they bring the film into discussion and create brand awareness that this is also a film,' Tuladhar adds, 'But for the film to run and last long, the film itself must be good. Once it is released, word-of-mouth publicity actually works.' He points out that promoting a film advertised as comedy by arresting actors like criminals is contrary to the subject matter.

'A film is a show business; we have to show what we have, but we shouldn't show just anything while showing it,' Tuladhar continues. 'It is better not to engage in wrong kinds of promotion.' He stresses the need to promote the film as much as possible and adopt creative styles in it.

Senior producer Sushil Pokharel says that while stunts can be used in film promotion, attention must be paid to whether they do good or bad.

'Promotion is about informing people about the film. Scandals or stunts are added to make people aware of the film,' Pokharel says. 'But publicity is of two types: 'good publicity' and 'bad publicity.' If the publicity is good and attractive, audiences will come to the hall, but if presented in a bad way, audiences will not come.' He argues that promotion stunts can be beneficial or backfire.

'The trend of stunts, scandals, and rumors is worldwide; it did not start only in Nepal. In any film industry worldwide, creating controversy and scandals has become a kind of culture in the film line,' Pokharel adds. 'Such promotion is not unique to 'Kakakiki' in Nepal; it has been happening in Hollywood and Bollywood as well.'

However, Pokharel advises that when doing such promotions, one must think carefully whether it will attract the audience or backfire. He believes that promotions should be done thoughtfully, sending a positive message to the audience like 'Wow, how good it is.'

'I personally don't like walking around the streets like a street circus. I feel that film promotion and publicity should have a certain standard,' Pokharel added. 'My belief is that promoting by making people run around the streets is cheap publicity, and cheap publicity should not be done.'

title: Preserving Nepal’s Cultural Heritage Through Open Knowledge: Wiki Loves Monuments 2026 - Wikimedia.org
description: Preserving Nepal’s Cultural Heritage Through Open Knowledge: Wiki Loves Monuments 2026  Wikimedia.org
publisher.title: Wikimedia.org
full_article:
Community-led photography, digital innovation and strategic partnerships are connecting Nepal’s historic monuments with a global audience.

Nepal’s cultural heritage from ancient temples and historic palaces to traditional courtyards and intricate stone sculptures reflects centuries of artistic achievement, cultural traditions and collective memory. Documenting and sharing this heritage is essential to increasing public awareness and ensuring that knowledge remains accessible to future generations.

Wiki Loves Monuments 2026 in Nepal, coordinated by Wikimedians of Nepal with UNESCO as a strategic partner, brought together photographers, volunteers, heritage enthusiasts and partner organizations to document Nepal’s built heritage and make photographs freely accessible worldwide.

Held from 1 September to 15 October 2026, the campaign demonstrated how community participation, photography and open knowledge can complement efforts to promote cultural heritage awareness and digital documentation.

A national campaign with global reach

Wiki Loves Monuments is an international photography competition that encourages people to document historic monuments and share their photographs through Wikimedia Commons, the free media repository supporting Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects.

Since its pilot in the Netherlands in 2010, the initiative has grown into a global movement. The international project reports more than 3.2 million photographs contributed by over 100,000 participants across 100 countries, illustrating approximately one million monuments. The initiative saw participation from 58 countries and territories across the world, demonstrating its international reach and commitment to documenting and preserving cultural heritage.

Nepal has participated since 2013, building a growing collection of photographs documenting the country’s monuments and historic places.The country’s campaign page reports a cumulative collection of approximately 25,900+ photographs contributed under Creative Commons licences through previous editions and the broader national initiative.

The 2026 Nepal campaign recorded 1,500+ photographs uploaded as of 15 October 2026, alongside more than 100 online/offline participants and engagement with 5+ partner organizations. These contributions expand the availability of visual resources about Nepal’s heritage and create opportunities for educational, research and public awareness activities.

Strategic partnerships for Heritage Awareness

Collaboration between Wikimedia communities, UNESCO and other heritage stakeholders offers opportunities to connect local heritage documentation with broader cultural awareness and educational objectives.

Through photography activities, outreach and community participation, the campaign encouraged people to explore historic places, appreciate traditional craftsmanship and contribute to a shared digital knowledge resource.

A highlight was the Bhaktapur Heritage and Photo Walk, held on 10 October 2026. Participants explored three historic areas: Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Taumadhi Square and Dattatreya Square. They documented monuments and architectural features, including the 55-Window Palace, Nyatapola Temple, Bhairav Temple and Dattatreya Temple.

The guided walk connected photography with learning about heritage, encouraging participants to see monuments not simply as photographic subjects but as important expressions of cultural identity and history.

Photographs from the walk contributed to the wider campaign collection on Wikimedia Commons, creating additional visual resources that can support the online documentation of Bhaktapur’s heritage.

Open licences, lasting knowledge

A defining feature of Wiki Loves Monuments is its commitment to freely licensed photography. Under the competition’s Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike requirements, photographs can be shared and adapted in accordance with the applicable licence terms.

For example, CC BY-SA 4.0 permits sharing and adaptation, including commercial reuse, provided users give appropriate attribution, link to the licence, indicate changes and comply with the licence’s share-alike requirements for adaptations.

Through Wikimedia Commons, these photographs can support Wikipedia articles, educational resources, publications and research, helping audiences discover Nepal’s heritage beyond geographical boundaries. Open licensing enables continued use of these resources while recognizing the photographers who created them.

Digital documentation does not replace physical conservation or official heritage records. Instead, it complements these efforts by improving access to visual information and encouraging wider public engagement with historic places.

Building a lasting legacy

The conclusion of the 2026 submission period marks an important milestone, but the photographs can continue contributing to public knowledge long after the competition ends. Reviewing submissions, recognizing outstanding work and improving image descriptions and categorization will help make the collection more useful and discoverable.

Wiki Loves Monuments 2026 in Nepal illustrates how community-led initiatives, strategic partnerships and open digital platforms can bring cultural heritage closer to people around the world.

By transforming individual photographs into freely accessible cultural resources, the campaign strengthens the connection between Nepal’s local heritage and global knowledge supporting learning, discovery and appreciation for future generations.

title: Croatia says unaware of violent pushback of migrants from Pakistan, Nepal and other countries - Arab News PK
description: Croatia says unaware of violent pushback of migrants from Pakistan, Nepal and other countries  Arab News PK
publisher.title: Arab News PK
full_article:
ZAGREB: Croatian authorities said on Saturday they had “no information” about claims that police severely beat dozens of migrants and pushed them back to Bosnia earlier this week.

Rights groups and independent media have repeatedly accused Croatian police of illegally forcing migrants back over the European Union’s external border, notably to Bosnia.

The authorities have generally denied such allegations.

Austrian humanitarian organization SOS Balkanroute said Croatian police had beaten and forcibly pushed back 53 migrants into Bosnia on Wednesday.

Five of the migrants sustained broken arms or legs and head injuries in the incident, it said in a statement released on Friday.

According to migrants’ accounts around 15 masked Croatian police officers beat anyone who moved, the organization said, calling it “one of the most brutal cases of border violence” it had documented in recent months.

Croatian Interior Minister Davor Bozinovic said on Saturday that police had only heard about the incident from media reports.

“We have no such information, nor have we received any official notification from the Bosnian authorities, primarily the police,” he said.

The organization’s founder Petar Rosandic said the incident was not isolated, describing violence at the EU’s external borders as “systematic.”

“This can no longer be swept under the rug by the Croatian authorities, the media, the EU and Austrian politicians,” he told AFP.

The 53 migrants — who came from Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Sudan and Pakistan — included three women and two children, the charity said. They were found in six separate groups along Bosnia’s northwestern border.

Croatia, which guards one of the EU’s longest external land borders, is a major transit country for undocumented migrants trying to enter the bloc through the Balkans.

EU border agency Frontex said more than 12,500 irregular border-crossing detections were recorded along the route last year, down 42 percent from 2024.

title: Nepal Bar Association Investigation Committee Faces Crisis - Ratopati
description: Nepal Bar Association Investigation Committee Faces Crisis  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. The committee formed by the Nepal Bar Association to investigate the case of Supreme Court judges and intermediaries has fallen into crisis without even starting its work. The investigation process has become uncertain after three members, including the committee's coordinator and former Bar President Chandreshwor Shrestha, refused to be on the committee.

The Bar had formed a six-member committee to investigate the controversy after some Supreme Court judges met and communicated via SMS with intermediary Inam Sapkota, and documents were leaked linking Chief Justice Dr. Manoj Kumar Sharma. The committee, formed under Shrestha's coordination, includes senior advocates Purnaman Shakya, Usha Malla Pathak, Surendra Kumar Mahato, and central member of the Bar Baburam Aryal as member-secretary. Although the committee was given a deadline of one month, 15 days have already passed without starting work.

Committee coordinator Shrestha is preparing to submit a letter to Bar President Vijayprasad Mishra on the upcoming Tuesday, refusing to be on the committee. He is stepping down as coordinator, considering the hardship of his clients, as he has many cases of his clients in the Supreme Court and would have to withdraw from arguing cases if he were on the investigation committee.

Committee member and senior advocate Purnaman Shakya has already submitted a letter to Bar President Mishra and refused to be on the committee. He stated that he could not serve on the committee as he was not consulted and would have to abandon the cases of clients he argues daily. 'After being on the investigation committee, we cannot argue cases until the investigation is complete,' Shakya told Ratopati. 'It's not just one, but talks of seven judges are coming up. After being on the investigation committee, on what moral grounds can we argue?'

Shakya argues that it is practically impossible to take statements from sitting judges, demand sources from journalists, and investigate the bank statement from America that is said to be of the Chief Justice. Recalling that the Bar had protested for more than 100 days regarding the issue of former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana, Shakya said that the Bar should be in a 'watchdog' role and keep a watch, and it is not necessary for it to take the initiative to investigate judges itself. He stated that the Bar can only exert pressure if any judge has proven corruption and has not resigned, and if an investigation is to be conducted, former judges or senior retired legal experts can be appointed.

Similarly, another committee member and senior advocate Surendra Mahato stated that he had informed the Bar President on the day after the committee was formed, i.e., on Kartik 17, that he could not serve on the committee.

Mahato stated that although he does not handle the cases of Deepak Bhatta and Rohit Gupta, he is the lawyer for another case connected to the root of the controversy, and due to 'conflict of interest,' it is not appropriate for him to be on the committee. He also expressed the opinion that the Bar should not form a committee as the matter of investigating judges is the responsibility of the judiciary itself.

With half of the committee's time elapsed since its formation and the situation of three members, including the coordinator, stepping down, the relevance of the Bar's investigation committee and its future course of action have become uncertain.
